findings.description: The 2026-11-02 correction did not reach FR-AUTH-006. FR-IAM-014 AC-11 (corrected) now says: 'setRoles throws new AuthRejection(422, "role_policy") after changePassword succeeded answers 503 with body code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and applied: ["password"], written by the A4 handler (the exception does not reach the FR-AUTH-006 AC-3 ErrorMiddleware)'. The statement adds that an AuthRejection or IllegalArgumentException after the password is answered by the A4 handler as 503. FR-AUTH-006 (statement, still evolving) lists only the DuplicateUserException, a false changePassword, an AuthUnavailableException and any other store exception as A4-handled, 'status and code as AC-3 gives them', then says 'every other exception in the auth routers goes through the AC-3 ErrorMiddleware'. FR-AUTH-006 AC-3 maps 'an AuthRejection with its own status and code'. Under FR-AUTH-006 the AC-11 case is a 422 from the ErrorMiddleware, and under FR-IAM-014 it is a 503 written by A4. Both cannot pass. The judgement lists this contradiction as resolved and misses the new one.
findings.suggested_action: Extend the A4 exception list in the FR-AUTH-006 statement with 'an AuthRejection or IllegalArgumentException after the password step (503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, FR-IAM-014 AC-11)'. Use a guarded SRS mutation in sdd mode, then re-judge FR-IAM-014 dependency/AC axes.

findings.description: The floor scope is narrower than the literal text of 00 R38. 00 R38 says '모든 실패 응답(503 포함, 429 제외 — 해시를 하지 않는다 …)은 요청 시작부터 max(1.25T, 실제 경과) + 0–50 ms 난수 지터 뒤에 보낸다'. The SEC-TOKEN-009 statement floors only attempts that reached step ④, and also exempts 403 transport/CSRF, 415, the 400 shape answer and the multiple-credential/API-key rejections. A store-error 503 from findByUsername at step ③ is not floored either, but no list names that case; the 'attempt' definition excludes it only by implication. The reading is defensible: none of these precede-hash answers depend on account existence. But 00 does not record it, and the judgement handles it only as a docs/api note in its conditions.
findings.suggested_action: Name the step-③ store-error 503 explicitly (floored or not) in the SEC-TOKEN-009 statement and record the 00 R38 interpretation in docs/api. An owner note in 00 would remove the literal mismatch.

findings.description: Two ACs pull against each other. AC-2 requires a SQL-text test that 'recordFailure issues an UPDATE ... SET <count> = <count> + 1 … rather than SELECT-then-UPDATE'. AC-6 (decided 2026-11-02) requires that 'the first failure after the window has passed resets the row to count 1 with a new window start in the same atomic statement', which needs a CASE on window_start. The research note says so ('reset or increment with a CASE'). A literal AC-2 text check for 'SET count = count + 1' fails on the CASE form.
findings.suggested_action: Reword AC-2 to assert a single atomic UPDATE/upsert with no preceding SELECT whose increment branch is count + 1, so the CASE reset form of AC-6 passes.

findings.description: The fixed counting window was decided only for the JDBC counters (FR-IAM-013 AC-6: 'fixed, not sliding … node clocks are used the same way as the in-memory throttle'). REL-FLOW-001 and IR-FLOW-003 do not state a window rule for the in-memory and file counters. The claimed sameness has no SRS backing, so a sliding in-memory window would make limits behave differently between SINGLE_INSTANCE and MULTI_INSTANCE deployments.
findings.suggested_action: State the window semantics for InMemoryLoginThrottle and the file counters (REL-FLOW-001 or IR-FLOW-003), or drop the 'same way as the in-memory throttle' claim.

findings.description: The judgement misses a condition about where lock state lives. The FR-FLOW-009 implementation notes say 'lock state stored with the throttle/device-trust storage defaults (REL-FLOW-001)'. REL-FLOW-001 and FR-IAM-013 define storage for throttle counters and device-token invalidation only, and there is no JDBC lock store. Under MULTI_INSTANCE a lock set or released (AC-5 DELETE) on one node has no specified shared storage. This does not block the single-node ACs, but no condition records it.
findings.suggested_action: Add a condition: implement the Lockout on LoginThrottle keys through the limit-argument methods, so JdbcLoginThrottle shares it and reset(key) releases it. Otherwise state the storage in FR-FLOW-009/REL-FLOW-001.

findings.description: AC-8 requires a real-adapter test where a failed login (JSON body) on TinyHttpd gets a 401 JSON answer after the floor. The NaruServe-tinyhttpd test classpath holds only testFixtures(project(':NaruServe-api')) (build.gradle:321-322), and the fixture StubJsonCodec throws on decode. The judgement's condition names Gson for the servlet test classpath (build.gradle:370) but not for TinyHttpd. This is not a blocker, because a test-only codec or dependency fixes it, but the condition is missing.
findings.suggested_action: Add the condition: give NaruServe-tinyhttpd tests a decoding JsonCodec (testImplementation project(':NaruServe-gson') or a test codec) for AC-8.

findings.description: AC-7 is hard to turn into a deterministic reflection test, for two reasons. (1) The statement's seam is 'authenticate(String username, char[] password, AuthEventContext ctx)', while AC-7 says the single abstract method 'takes a username String and a char[] password', which leaves open whether ctx is allowed. (2) 'no public type or Auth builder option accepts a replacement for the Bearer or the API key authenticator' cannot be decided by reflection while the public TokenCodec SPI (IR-TOKEN-002) changes Bearer verification.
findings.suggested_action: Fix the exact parameter list in AC-7, or say 'whose parameters include', and name the builder options to check, excluding TokenCodec explicitly.

findings.description: The SEC-TOKEN-009 statement says 'Every password login attempt shall … run exactly one PBKDF2 computation'. IR-TOKEN-001 makes the password authenticator replaceable through the public Authenticator SPI (AC-1), for example for LDAP (00 §2), and such an authenticator runs no PBKDF2. Neither block says whether the one-PBKDF2 rule or only the floor applies when a custom Authenticator is set. The IR-TOKEN-001 note says only that 'the timing equalizer wraps the authenticator call'.
findings.suggested_action: Scope the one-PBKDF2 rule to the built-in password authenticator in SEC-TOKEN-009 or IR-TOKEN-001, and state that the slot and the floor still apply to a custom Authenticator.

findings.description: Parts of the judgement are stale. For FR-FLOW-009 and FR-IAM-014 the text was corrected on 2026-11-02 (blockers_resolved: 'SRS corrected 2026-11-02 to follow 00'). Yet the conditions still read 'Resolve the AC-5 / SEC-FLOW-012 AC-6 release semantics against 00 §6.4 … before implementation' and 'Resolve AC-11 and the statement's audit rule against 00 R37 14판 before implementation'. contradictions_found is still filled, and ac_verifiability stays at 10 for a contradiction that no longer holds. The label is not affected (83 stays high). The FR-FLOW-009 AC-5 and SEC-FLOW-012 AC-6 text now matches 00 §6.4 'R34 × 새 기기 admin' ('다른 관리자가 lockout 해제').
findings.suggested_action: Remove the stale 'resolve before implementation' conditions, move the old contradictions to history, and re-score ac_verifiability. For FR-IAM-014, record the new FR-AUTH-006 contradiction (F01) in its place.

findings.description: AC-6 says only that 'PATCH /auth/me carrying a username field does not change the username'. It does not fix the answer (field ignored with 200, or 400 BAD_REQUEST like the non-allowed attribute of AC-3). A test can assert only that nothing changed, so the client-visible behaviour is open.
findings.suggested_action: Fix the AC-6 answer, either 400 BAD_REQUEST (consistent with AC-3 and 00 R30 input checks) or 200 with the field ignored, and record it in docs/api.

findings.description: evidence_strength is 15/20 based only on 'code_context.json trace_validation FR-IAM-014'. The only trace is an addition site, utils/auth/Auth.java, which does not exist yet. The block's own implementation notes place the A4 handler in the adminRoutes() router (IR-IAM-005), not Auth.java, so the addition site is not the concrete site. FR-FLOW-006 got 13 for a similar directory-only trace.
findings.suggested_action: Lower evidence_strength (to about 12–13) or point the trace at the admin router class. The label stays high either way (score of about 80–81).

findings.description: Decided values still carry stale '[INFERRED] (name not final)' markers: FR-FLOW-009 AC-2 'Lockout.after(5).forMinutes(15) (name not final) [INFERRED:med:advisory]' (decided Q120), and FR-FLOW-006 AC-2 body shape '[INFERRED:med:advisory]' (decided Q51).
findings.suggested_action: Drop the markers when the docs/api pages are written. The judgement already lists this as a condition.

findings.description: IR-AUTH-003 AC-3 cites '(FR-FLOW-009 AC-2; 00 R34 (4))' for 'The Lockout login refusal … is the wrong-password answer invalid_credentials 401'. 00 R34 (4) says only that hard lock is opt-in, not applied to trusted devices, and released by DELETE. It names no response. The value comes from the 2026-11-02 decision Q54/Q55/Q120.
findings.suggested_action: Cite the decision (Q54/Q55/Q120) instead of R34 (4).

findings.description: IR-AUTH-003 AC-4 describes the A4-written 503 as 'written by the admin PATCH A4 handler with its applied list for a store failure of its steps'. Since the FR-IAM-014 AC-11 correction, A4 also writes a 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE for a non-store AuthRejection or IllegalArgumentException after the password. The code stays SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, so there is no conflict on the code, only an incomplete description.
findings.suggested_action: Add 'or an AuthRejection/IllegalArgumentException after the password step (FR-IAM-014 AC-11)'.

findings.description: The IR-IAM-005 research note still reads 'Open: success status of DELETE /users/:id/lockout … not fixed', while FR-FLOW-009 AC-5 decided 204 on 2026-11-02.
findings.suggested_action: Append a dated note in IR-IAM-005 pointing to FR-FLOW-009 AC-5 (204).

findings.description: The decision list and the blocks wrote different values. Q15 says 'wrong or missing setup token → 401 invalid_setup_token', while SEC-AUTH-003 AC-2 answers a missing or non-string token with 400 BAD_REQUEST, which follows 00 R30 24판. Q118 says 'Secure (except local DEV)', while SEC-FLOW-013 AC-10 says 'Secure present exactly when req.isSecure() is true'. In both cases the SRS text is the source of truth and is consistent with 00 and SEC-FLOW-009 AC-4.
findings.suggested_action: Annotate the decision list so it matches the SRS, so docs/api authors do not copy the list values.

findings.description: The AC-9 (a) fixture is 'update() applies the rename but silently does not apply the hash change', yet the AC asserts 'the password hash and ver are unchanged'. The SINGLE_INSTANCE default changePassword writes hash and ver++ in one update(), so the fixture must also drop the ver change, and the text does not say so.
findings.suggested_action: Say the fixture ignores the password_hash and ver fields of that update().

findings.description: The mapping is correct. policy-resolved.json is the default policy, every judgement has has_verification false and feasibility high, so the rule 'high → evolving' applies, and no stable or frozen is proposed. On promotion, though, all 12 blocks keep the heading suffix '[DRAFT — pending decision]' and the tag 'feasibility:medium', which will be stale.
findings.suggested_action: Update the tag to feasibility:high and the heading suffix with the stability change. The heading needs a guarded mutation, and requirement IDs must not change.
